chunks: And from him, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding a woman who was ignorant that she should pelt the Jamarah, until she departed to Mecca?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let her return and let her pelt the Jamarah, just as she was pelting; and for the man, it is like that (as well).'

key_terms.الْجِمَارَ: The Jamarah, the stone pillars in Mina stoned during Hajj
key_terms.فَلْتَرْجِعْ: So let her return (to the point of omission)
key_terms.نَفَرَتْ: Departed/moved quickly (referring to leaving the stoning site)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who forgets to stone the Jamarah pillars during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for a pilgrim who, due to ignorance or forgetfulness, missed stoning the Jamarah pillars, ruling that they must return to the point of omission and complete the ritual rather than restarting. This emphasizes the Shia jurisprudential principle of continuity in Hajj rites, ensuring the validity of the pilgrimage without imposing undue hardship on those who err unintentionally. The equal application to men and women highlights the universality of this legal ease within the ritual framework.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws, ‘What are youasws saying regarding a woman who was ignorant (of the fact) that she should be pelting the Jamarah, until she went to Makkah?’ Heasws said: ‘So let her return and let her pelt the Jamarah, just as she would have pelted; and (for) the men, it is like that (as well)’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from him (narrator of previous Hadith) from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who is ignorant of throwing pebbles until she leaves Makkah. He (the Imam) said, ‘She must return to throw pebbles as she was required to throw and the same rule applies to man.’”
